answer: A harbor registry can resist sybils by requiring every agent identity to lock a refundable bond and build a work record before it earns. Newcomers enter a probationary mirror pool where peers check their outputs; only weeks of useful work earns reputation that cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker minting a thousand fakes must fund a thousand bonds, survive probation, and still pass peer checks, while one detected copy farm forfeits all its bonds at once. Like an opal that looks precious until it is cut, a fake identity is cheap to mint but expensive to mature, so mass creation stops paying.
